pregunta: How can executives measure whether an AI agent is delivering business value beyond saving employees time?
respuesta: Measure outcomes against a pre-agent baseline or control group: incremental revenue or conversion, customer satisfaction and retention, fewer errors or compliance incidents, lower cost per transaction, and faster resolution. For example, a retailer can track whether an agent improves product recommendations and reduces returns—not just staff hours saved. Include the full cost of deployment, oversight, and ongoing maintenance, then calculate net value and payback. Review results by task and customer segment to identify where the agent creates measurable impact.

pregunta: What does fine-tuning a generative AI model actually change, and how is it different from simply giving the model better instructions?
respuesta: Fine-tuning updates a model’s internal weights using examples, making it more likely to respond in a particular style or handle recurring tasks—for example, classifying customer-service requests using a company’s categories. Better instructions change what the model is asked to do at runtime; they don’t change the model itself. Instructions are quicker to revise and suit changing needs. Fine-tuning takes data and testing, and is useful when consistent behavior is needed across many requests.

pregunta: Can you show how to structure a prompt that summarizes monthly sales data for executives and highlights unusual changes?
respuesta:
Use this prompt template:

“You are a sales analyst preparing a monthly executive brief. Analyze the sales data below and summarize: (1) total sales and change versus the previous month and the same month last year; (2) top-performing and underperforming products, regions, and channels; (3) unusual changes, defined as month-over-month movements above [X%] or outside the usual range. For each unusual change, state its size, likely context, and what to investigate. Distinguish facts from hypotheses, flag missing data, and do not invent explanations. Use concise bullets and end with up to three recommended actions.

Data: [paste data]”

pregunta: If we fine-tune a model on outdated procedures, how difficult is it to update its behavior when our processes change?
respuesta: If procedures are embedded through fine-tuning, updates usually require new examples, another fine-tuning run, and testing—old behavior may still surface. For frequently changing processes, keep the authoritative procedures in a versioned knowledge base the model retrieves at answer time. Then, for example, updating a new approval workflow can be as simple as replacing the relevant document, followed by a quick validation.

pregunta: Could a mining company in Chile use RAG to help technicians find relevant safety procedures and equipment manuals, even when they ask questions in everyday language?
respuesta: Yes. A Chilean mining company could use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to match technicians’ everyday questions—such as “What should I check before servicing this pump?”—to relevant, approved safety procedures and equipment manuals, then summarize the guidance with source references. Keeping documents current, restricting access appropriately, and requiring escalation to qualified personnel for high-risk or unclear cases helps reduce the chance of unsafe or outdated advice.

pregunta: What are common mistakes companies make when preparing training examples for fine-tuning?
respuesta: Common mistakes include using inconsistent labels or answer formats, relying on low-quality or outdated examples, and including too few examples to cover real-world cases. Companies may also overrepresent easy or common requests, omit edge cases, or mix conflicting policies—for example, different rules for refund approvals. Other pitfalls are leaking personal or confidential data, using examples that do not match the model’s intended use, and failing to separate training examples from evaluation data. Fine-tuning works best with accurate, representative, consistently formatted examples.

pregunta: What are common mistakes companies make when using user satisfaction scores to evaluate generative AI systems?
respuesta: Common mistakes include treating average satisfaction as proof of accuracy, safety, or business value; relying on ratings from a small or biased set of users; ignoring nonresponses and differences in task difficulty; comparing systems without controlling for prompts, model versions, or user groups; and optimizing for agreeable answers rather than truthful, useful ones. For example, a chatbot may score well because it sounds confident while giving incorrect advice. Pair satisfaction scores with task success, factuality, safety, and operational metrics.

pregunta: Which metrics should a Chilean retailer track to assess an AI assistant that answers questions about product availability and delivery?
respuesta: Track: answer accuracy against live inventory and delivery data; availability and ETA accuracy by store, comuna, and region; task completion and first-contact resolution; escalation and repeat-contact rates; response time; customer satisfaction; and business impact such as product conversion and cart abandonment. Monitor incorrect promises, especially unavailable stock or missed delivery dates, as critical safety metrics.

pregunta: How can we assess whether fine-tuning is worth the cost for a Chilean retailer handling seasonal customer inquiries?
respuesta: Run a time-boxed pilot on representative peak-season inquiries in Chilean Spanish. Compare the base model, retrieval or prompt improvements, and a fine-tuned model on answer accuracy, policy compliance, escalation rate, response time, and customer satisfaction. Estimate total costs—training, evaluation, maintenance, and peak-period inference—and quantify benefits such as fewer agent minutes and fewer incorrect resolutions. Fine-tune only if it materially outperforms simpler options and projected seasonal savings exceed those costs; otherwise, use retrieval or prompts and reassess when inquiry patterns change.

pregunta: What safeguards and evaluation steps should we put in place before letting an LLM draft responses about Chilean tax or labor rules?
respuesta: Ground drafts in current, versioned Chilean primary sources (e.g., Servicio de Impuestos Internos, Dirección del Trabajo, and legislation), with citations and effective dates. Require qualified Chilean tax or labor professionals to review high-impact or ambiguous cases; clearly label outputs as drafts, not legal advice, and provide escalation paths. Protect personal and payroll data, restrict access, and log source versions and approvals. Before launch, test representative and edge cases with local experts for factual accuracy, citation support, date sensitivity, and appropriate refusal or escalation. Monitor errors and re-evaluate after legal or model updates.

pregunta: Could an AI agent help a Chilean retailer manage inventory across stores, and what data would it need?
respuesta: Yes. An AI agent could forecast demand by store, flag likely stockouts or excess inventory, and recommend transfers or replenishment orders—subject to manager approval. It would need reliable SKU-level sales and current stock data, purchase orders, supplier lead times and constraints, store capacity, pricing and promotions, and relevant calendars such as holidays. Weather or local events can improve forecasts. For example, it could move popular products between Santiago stores before a promotion while accounting for delivery times.

pregunta: How do AI agents use generative AI models, tools, and company data to complete a task from start to finish?
respuesta: An AI agent first interprets the goal and breaks it into steps. It uses a generative AI model to reason and draft responses, retrieves relevant company data—such as approved policies or customer records—and calls tools like email, CRM, or ERP systems to take action. It checks results, adjusts if needed, and continues until the task is complete. For example, it could review a customer request, check inventory, prepare a quote, and send it for human approval before issuing it.

pregunta: How can we evaluate whether a prompt consistently produces useful results before rolling it out across our company?
respuesta: Build a test set of representative business tasks, including edge cases and sensitive scenarios. Define what “useful” means—such as accuracy, completeness, tone, and policy compliance—and have reviewers score outputs against those criteria. Test the prompt repeatedly, since results can vary, and compare it with your current approach. Revise it based on failures, then pilot with a small group and monitor quality, user feedback, and risks before company-wide rollout. Keep the prompt versioned so changes can be retested.

pregunta: What privacy and regulatory risks should a Chilean company consider before using customer data to fine-tune a model?
respuesta: Under Chile’s current Law 19.628—and Law 21.719, effective December 1, 2026—check that model training has a valid legal basis and is compatible with the purpose customers were told about. Assess consent, sensitive data, customer rights, retention, security, and cross-border transfers. Removing names may not prevent re-identification; models can also memorize or reveal training data. Set vendor limits on reuse and deletion, and test for leakage. Financial, health, and other regulated sectors may have additional requirements. Obtain Chilean legal advice before processing.

pregunta: How could a Chilean retailer use RAG to help customer-service agents answer questions about product availability, returns, and delivery policies?
respuesta: A Chilean retailer could connect a RAG assistant to live inventory by store, delivery-region data, and approved return and shipping policies. When an agent asks a question, it retrieves relevant, up-to-date records and drafts a concise answer—for example, whether a product is available in a Santiago branch or how returns work for an online purchase. The agent can see the supporting sources before replying. If inventory is unavailable or policies conflict, the system should flag uncertainty and direct the agent to verify rather than guess.

pregunta: What are hallucinations, and how can a company reduce the risk of an LLM inventing details in a response about a product or policy?
respuesta: Hallucinations are plausible-sounding statements an LLM generates that are false or unsupported. To reduce risk, ground responses in current, approved product and policy documents using retrieval; instruct the model to answer only from those sources and say when information is unavailable; include source citations; and test common questions. Require human review for high-impact or ambiguous cases, and regularly update the source material.

pregunta: How can we ask a model to analyze a business problem without exposing confidential company or customer information?
respuesta: Describe the problem using abstract or aggregated details, and replace names, account numbers, exact dates, and unique events with generic labels or ranges. For example, ask about “a retailer with declining repeat purchases” rather than naming your company or customers. Use synthetic examples where possible, and check that combined details cannot identify anyone. For sensitive analysis, use an approved enterprise AI environment with appropriate data protections; never paste confidential information into an unapproved model.

pregunta: What are practical ways to build a reliable evaluation set from customer questions while protecting personal data?
respuesta: Collect questions only under an approved purpose and retention policy. Remove names, contact details, account numbers, and other identifiers; redact sensitive details before review, and restrict access to authorized evaluators. Use aggregation or synthetic examples when real wording is unnecessary. Sample across customer segments, topics, languages, and difficulty levels; avoid overrepresenting frequent users. Have domain experts label expected answers and safety requirements, resolve disagreements, and keep a versioned, held-out test set. Regularly check for privacy leaks, bias, and performance drift, and delete data when no longer needed.

pregunta: Could we fine-tune a model to draft responses in our company’s brand voice in Chilean Spanish? What examples would we need to provide?
respuesta: Yes. Fine-tuning can teach a model to draft in your brand voice and natural Chilean Spanish. Provide paired examples of the original request or context and the approved response, covering common use cases (sales, support, marketing), channels, formality levels, Chilean vocabulary, and how to handle complaints or sensitive topics. Include examples of what to avoid and relevant brand guidelines. Use high-quality, consistent examples; remove personal or confidential information. A representative set across real scenarios is more useful than many near-duplicates.

pregunta: If an AI gives us a plausible but incorrect answer, how can we revise the prompt to reduce the risk of similar mistakes?
respuesta: Add the relevant context and constraints, specify what counts as a reliable source, and ask the AI to distinguish verified facts from assumptions. Tell it to say when information is missing rather than guess, and request citations or a step-by-step check for important claims. For example: “Use only the attached sales data; don’t infer missing figures. Flag any uncertainty and cite the row supporting each conclusion.”

pregunta: How can we test whether a retrieval-augmented chatbot is using the right internal documents rather than inventing answers?
respuesta: Build a test set of realistic business questions with the correct internal documents and expected answers. For each test, check whether retrieval returns the right document, whether the answer is supported by its cited passages, and whether the chatbot says “I don’t know” when the documents lack an answer. Include outdated, conflicting, and misleading documents, and track retrieval accuracy, citation accuracy, and unsupported-claim rates. For example, test whether a policy question cites the current HR policy—not an old version.

pregunta: What is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and how is it different from simply asking a large language model to answer from its training data?
respuesta: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) first searches trusted, up-to-date sources—such as a company’s policies, product documents, or Chilean regulations—then gives that information to a large language model to generate an answer. Unlike answering from training data alone, RAG can use private or recent information, provide source references, and reduce outdated or unsupported answers. It does not retrain the model, and its accuracy still depends on finding relevant, reliable sources.

pregunta: How should we measure whether a generative AI assistant is actually reducing call-handling time at a Chilean bank without making its answers less accurate?
respuesta: Run a randomized, agent-level pilot: eligible calls are handled with or without the assistant, balanced by call type, language, and complexity. Compare average total handling time—including talk, hold, and after-call work—while measuring accuracy through blinded audits against bank policy and records, plus critical-error and customer-resolution rates. Set an accuracy non-inferiority threshold before launch; adopt only if time falls and accuracy stays within that threshold. Track results by product and customer segment, and monitor complaints and repeat calls for several weeks.

pregunta: What are tokens and context windows, and how could they affect the cost or usefulness of summarizing long reports?
respuesta: Tokens are the chunks of text an AI processes; a context window is the maximum number it can handle at once, including the report, instructions, and response. Longer reports use more tokens, which can raise costs or exceed that limit. If a report is too long, the AI may miss sections or require it to be split and summarized in stages. For example, summarizing a lengthy annual report in sections can manage limits, but may lose connections between topics unless the summaries are combined and checked.

pregunta: What are the main risks of giving an AI agent permission to access company systems or take actions on its own?
respuesta: Key risks include exposing confidential customer or financial data, taking incorrect or unauthorized actions (such as changing records or approving payments), and being manipulated by malicious instructions hidden in emails or documents. Excessive permissions can turn a small mistake into a major incident. Poor logging may make actions hard to trace, while failures can disrupt operations or breach privacy and regulatory obligations. Limit access to what the agent needs, require human approval for high-impact actions, and monitor and audit its activity.

pregunta: How should we compare the performance of a fine-tuned model with our current support team before deciding to deploy it?
respuesta: Run a controlled pilot using representative, anonymized support cases. Have the model and your team handle the same cases, then compare resolution accuracy, customer satisfaction, response and resolution time, escalation rates, policy compliance, and cost per resolved case. Use human reviewers who don’t know which response came from whom, and assess high-risk cases separately. Track performance by issue type and customer segment. Set minimum quality and safety thresholds before testing; deploy gradually only if results meet them, with human fallback and ongoing monitoring.

pregunta: How does retrieval-augmented generation differ from fine-tuning, and which approach might suit a company that needs answers based on frequently updated procedures?
respuesta: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fetches relevant information from current documents at answer time, while fine-tuning changes a model’s behavior by training it on examples. For frequently updated procedures, RAG is usually a better fit: update the document store rather than retrain the model. It can also provide source references, helping employees verify answers.

pregunta: Would fine-tuning help a Chilean bank classify customer service requests more accurately, or should we start with a simpler approach?
respuesta: Start with a simpler approach: use a strong pretrained model with clear instructions, a defined set of request categories, and a representative test set in Chilean Spanish. This is faster and cheaper, and may handle requests such as card blocks, transfers, and account inquiries well. Measure accuracy by category and review errors with service staff. Consider fine-tuning only if performance remains inadequate on frequent, distinctive requests and you have enough properly labeled, privacy-protected examples. Keep human review for sensitive or ambiguous cases.

pregunta: How can we prompt a model to adapt the same product announcement for Chilean customers, internal staff, and investors?
respuesta: Use one prompt that supplies the announcement’s verified facts and asks for three versions: Chilean customers (benefits, local relevance, clear call to action), internal staff (what changes, how to respond, where to get help), and investors (business impact, milestones, and measurable outcomes). Specify Chilean Spanish, suitable tone and length for each audience, and require the model to preserve facts, avoid unsupported claims, and flag missing information.

pregunta: What kinds of company documents should we prepare before building a RAG system, and how much effort does cleaning them usually take?
respuesta: Prepare the documents people need to query: policies and procedures, product or service manuals, contracts and approved templates, customer-support knowledge, technical documentation, and relevant reports. Include ownership, dates, version status, and access permissions. Cleaning effort varies: well-organized, searchable files may need only days of review; scattered, duplicated, outdated, or scanned documents can take weeks. In many projects, document preparation is a significant early effort—often around 20–40% of the work. Start with a focused, high-value collection rather than digitizing everything.

pregunta: If an LLM gives a confident but incorrect answer about Chilean tax rules, what does that reveal about its limitations?
respuesta: It reveals that an LLM can generate plausible-sounding answers without reliably verifying facts. It may lack current, complete knowledge of Chilean tax law and can confuse rules or omit exceptions. Treat its output as a starting point—not tax advice—and verify it against official sources or a qualified Chilean tax professional.

pregunta: What is a large language model, and how does it generate a response when a customer asks a question?
respuesta: A large language model (LLM) is an AI system trained on large amounts of text to recognize language patterns. When a customer asks a question, it processes the words and context, then generates a reply one piece at a time by predicting what is likely to come next. For example, a bank’s chatbot might use an LLM to explain a fee in plain language, while relying on approved company information to keep the answer relevant and accurate.

pregunta: What does LLMOps involve beyond deploying a model, and how would it apply to a mining company’s internal knowledge assistant?
respuesta: LLMOps covers the ongoing operation of an AI system—not just deploying its model. It includes managing knowledge sources and updates, testing answer quality and safety, controlling access, monitoring performance and costs, tracking versions, and handling user feedback and incidents. For a mining company’s internal assistant, this means keeping safety procedures, maintenance manuals, and operating standards current; restricting answers by role or site; checking that responses cite reliable sources; testing high-risk questions; and monitoring errors so teams can improve the system before incorrect guidance affects operations.

pregunta: How could a mining company in Chile use AI agents to reduce equipment downtime without compromising worker safety?
respuesta: AI agents can combine sensor data from haul trucks, crushers, and mills with maintenance logs to predict failures and flag abnormal conditions early. They can prioritize inspections, check parts availability, and propose maintenance windows that minimize production disruption. At remote Chilean sites, agents can coordinate alerts and work orders across teams despite connectivity constraints. Keep safety-critical decisions under human control: require qualified workers to verify recommendations, follow lockout/tagout procedures, and never let an agent override equipment interlocks or authorize work in hazardous areas.

pregunta: How can we detect when an AI assistant’s answer quality declines after we update its prompts, documents, or underlying model?
respuesta: Maintain a representative set of real business questions with expert-approved answers, then test it before and after each prompt, document, or model update. Compare accuracy, relevance, completeness, citation quality, and safety; use automated checks where possible and human review for nuanced cases. Track results by topic and user group, and set thresholds that block or flag releases when quality drops. In production, sample conversations, monitor user feedback and escalation rates, and regularly rerun the tests—for example, on a Chilean bank’s customer-service questions.

pregunta: Can a fine-tuned model work well across different Chilean regions and customer groups, or could the training data introduce bias?
respuesta: A fine-tuned model can work across Chilean regions and customer groups, but it is not guaranteed. If training data underrepresents certain regions, age groups, or ways of speaking, the model may perform worse or produce biased responses. Use representative, consented data; test performance separately by region and customer group; review failures with local teams; and monitor results after launch. For example, check whether customer-service answers work equally well for people in Santiago and rural areas.

pregunta: Would RAG or fine-tuning be a better way for a Chilean bank to make an AI assistant respond using its internal procedures, and why?
respuesta: RAG is usually the better choice: it retrieves answers from current, approved internal procedures, which can change frequently, and can provide source references for auditability. A Chilean bank can also enforce document-level access controls and update content without retraining the model. Fine-tuning is better for consistent tone or task behavior, not for storing procedures. The bank may combine both, with strong security, evaluation, and human escalation for high-risk cases.

pregunta: If our documents contain conflicting policies or outdated versions, how can a RAG system identify which source to trust?
respuesta: A RAG system should use explicit source metadata and governance rules—not similarity alone. Rank documents by authority, approval status, effective date, version, and business scope; for example, prefer the current HR policy approved by Legal over an older draft. Detect and flag conflicting passages, cite the sources used, and abstain or request human review when rules do not resolve the conflict. Keep documents versioned and regularly remove or mark superseded content.

pregunta: What is a realistic first pilot for AI agents at a Chilean energy company, and how should we evaluate it?
respuesta: Pilot an agent that helps maintenance planners prioritize distribution-network work orders. It can search asset history, outage records, weather, and approved procedures, then draft a prioritized work plan with cited sources for a human to approve. Keep it read-only initially; do not let it dispatch crews or change equipment settings. Test it on historical cases, then a small live team. Compare planning time, prioritization accuracy, citation quality, safety or compliance exceptions, user adoption, and cost against today’s process. Set stop/go thresholds before launch and require human approval throughout.

pregunta: How could a bank use AI agents to support customer service while meeting Chilean privacy and regulatory requirements?
respuesta: Use agents for routine queries—such as explaining fees, checking application status, or guiding customers through card controls—while requiring strong authentication and human approval for sensitive or consequential actions. Give each agent access only to data needed for its task; apply purpose limits, retention controls, encryption, access logging, and clear disclosure that customers are interacting with AI. Do not use customer conversations to train models without an appropriate legal basis and safeguards. Assess vendors and cross-border data flows, preserve bank secrecy, and align controls with Chile’s privacy laws and applicable CMF requirements, including cybersecurity, outsourcing, and audit obligations.

pregunta: What common mistakes do companies make when deploying AI agents, and how can we avoid them?
respuesta: Common mistakes include giving agents vague goals, excessive autonomy, poor access to company data, and no reliable way to test results. Companies also deploy agents without integrating them into real workflows or defining who handles failures. Start with a narrow, measurable task—such as classifying customer inquiries—connect only approved data and tools, set clear permissions and escalation rules, and test against realistic cases. Keep human review for consequential decisions, monitor quality and cost, and expand only when the agent delivers measurable business value.

pregunta: What is prompt engineering, and why should executives at a Chilean company care about it?
respuesta: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing clear instructions, context, and examples so generative AI produces more useful, reliable outputs. Executives should care because better prompts can improve productivity and reduce errors in tasks such as drafting customer responses, summarizing reports, or analyzing sales data. For a Chilean company, prompts can specify local terminology, Spanish-language tone, regulatory constraints, and business context—helping teams get more relevant results while keeping human review and data privacy in place.

pregunta: How should we monitor latency and token costs for an AI tool used by customer service teams across Chile?
respuesta: Track end-to-end latency (median and p95), model latency, timeouts, and tool errors; set alerts against customer-service SLAs. Record input/output tokens and estimated cost per conversation and resolved case, segmented by channel, team, model, and time of day. Dashboard trends alongside resolution rate and escalation rate so cheaper or faster responses are not mistaken for better service. Convert costs to CLP for budgeting, review usage during Chilean peak hours, and use privacy-safe logs with conversation IDs rather than unnecessary customer data.

pregunta: What is the difference between evaluating an LLM before launch and monitoring it in production, and why do we need both?
respuesta: Pre-launch evaluation tests an LLM in controlled conditions against defined criteria—such as accuracy, safety, cost, and performance—before customers rely on it. Production monitoring tracks its behavior on real interactions over time, detecting issues such as changing user needs, data drift, latency, or rising costs. We need both: testing reduces launch risk, while monitoring catches problems tests cannot predict. For example, a bank may validate a customer-service assistant before release, then monitor live responses for errors or emerging complaints.

pregunta: How do AI agents differ from traditional automation tools such as robotic process automation?
respuesta: Traditional RPA follows predefined rules to repeat structured tasks—for example, copying invoice data between systems. AI agents can interpret goals, handle less-structured information, choose tools or next steps, and adapt when conditions change. For a Chilean retailer, an agent might investigate a delayed supplier order by checking emails and inventory systems, then recommend or take an approved action. Agents are more flexible, but their outputs can be less predictable, so they need controls and human oversight.

pregunta: How does RAG handle information that changes frequently, such as prices, inventory, or updated compliance policies?
respuesta: RAG retrieves relevant information from connected sources when a question is asked, rather than relying only on what the model learned during training. For frequently changing data—such as prices, inventory, or compliance policies—connect it to an up-to-date source of truth, using live queries or frequent index updates. This helps answers reflect current information without retraining the model. For example, a retailer can have RAG check its inventory system before answering whether an item is in stock.

pregunta: If our AI assistant gives different answers to the same question, how can we decide whether that variability is acceptable for our business?
respuesta: Judge variability by business impact, not by whether wording changes. Define acceptable boundaries: answers may vary in tone or examples, but must preserve facts, policies, and required actions. Test representative questions repeatedly and measure factual accuracy, policy compliance, and downstream outcomes. Set stricter thresholds for high-risk uses—such as pricing, legal, or customer commitments—and require human review where errors could cause harm. For low-risk tasks like brainstorming, broader variation may be useful. Document thresholds and monitor them as the model or business rules change.

pregunta: How should we compare two LLMs for summarizing insurance claims when one is cheaper but may omit important details?
respuesta: Evaluate both models on a representative, de-identified set of Chilean claims, including complex and high-value cases. Have claims experts compare summaries against source documents, scoring factual accuracy and omissions by severity—especially missing coverage, liability, injuries, or deadlines. Track critical-error rates, not just average quality, and test consistency across claim types. Choose the cheaper model only if it meets predefined safety thresholds; otherwise use it for low-risk claims and route complex cases to the stronger model or human reviewers.

pregunta: Why might the same prompt produce different answers, and how can we make outputs more consistent for a business process?
respuesta: The same prompt can produce different answers because generative AI samples from likely next words; results may also vary with model updates or changing context. For a business process, use a fixed model version, lower randomness (temperature), standardized prompts and inputs, and clear output formats. Add examples, validation rules, and automated checks—for instance, require invoice data in a fixed JSON schema. Monitor results and route exceptions for human review.

pregunta: How is an LLM different from a traditional business analytics model that predicts sales or customer churn?
respuesta: A traditional analytics model is built to predict a specific outcome—such as next month’s sales or whether a customer will churn—from structured data. An LLM is trained to understand and generate language, so it can summarize reports, answer questions, draft customer communications, or help analyze information in context. For example, a sales model forecasts revenue; an LLM can explain the forecast in plain English. LLMs are flexible, but their responses can be inaccurate, so important decisions still need validation.

pregunta: What does it mean when people say an LLM predicts the next token, and why does that matter for business users?
respuesta: An LLM generates text one piece at a time. Given the words so far, it estimates which next token—a word or word fragment—is most likely, then repeats this process. This is why it can draft emails, summarize documents, or answer questions, but it is not simply retrieving verified facts or reasoning like a person. For business users, outputs can be useful and fluent yet still contain errors, so important claims should be checked and sensitive decisions should retain human oversight.

pregunta: Can fine-tuning make a model reliably follow our compliance rules, or would we still need human review and other safeguards?
respuesta: Fine-tuning can improve consistency on familiar compliance tasks, but it cannot guarantee that a model will always follow the rules—especially when policies change or cases are unusual. Keep safeguards such as policy checks, access controls, ongoing testing and monitoring, and human review for high-impact decisions. For example, a Chilean bank might use a fine-tuned model to draft customer responses, while requiring staff approval before sending responses involving regulated advice.

pregunta: What common mistake do executives make when assuming an LLM can automate an entire workflow just because it can draft emails and summarize documents?
respuesta: They confuse strong language skills with end-to-end operational capability. Drafting emails or summarizing documents doesn’t mean an LLM can reliably access systems, make policy-compliant decisions, handle exceptions, or complete actions without checks. For example, summarizing a supplier invoice is not the same as validating it, approving payment, and updating finance records.

pregunta: How does giving a generative AI model a role, context, and examples change the quality of its response?
respuesta: A role sets the model’s perspective and tone; context supplies relevant goals, constraints, and business details; examples show the desired format and level of detail. Together, they make responses more relevant, consistent, and actionable—for example, asking it to act as a Chilean retail analyst and providing sales data can yield a more useful business summary. They guide the response but do not guarantee factual accuracy, so important claims should be checked.

pregunta: How should we prompt an AI assistant to compare two supplier proposals while separating facts from assumptions?
respuesta: Provide both proposals and ask the assistant to compare them against explicit criteria, such as price, delivery, service levels, and risk. Require a table with: (1) facts, each tied to a proposal and page or section; (2) assumptions or inferences, clearly labeled with their basis; and (3) missing information or questions for suppliers. Instruct it not to fill gaps or treat claims as verified, and to flag conflicting or incomparable terms. Ask for a recommendation only after the evidence and assumptions are separated.

pregunta: How can we keep a RAG assistant from showing confidential information to employees who are not authorized to see it?
respuesta: Enforce permissions before retrieval, not just in the prompt. Identify each employee, filter documents by their access rights, and recheck permissions when they change. Apply the same controls to search indexes, cached answers, citations, and connected systems. Test with accounts that have different roles—for example, ensure a sales employee cannot retrieve HR salary records—and monitor access for unusual activity.

pregunta: What are the most common reasons a RAG pilot gives inaccurate answers, even when the correct information exists in our documents?
respuesta: Common causes include poor document parsing (tables, PDFs, or scanned pages lose structure); chunking that separates facts from their context; retrieval settings or embeddings that miss company-specific terms; incorrect metadata filters; and ambiguous questions. The right passage may be retrieved but then buried, truncated, or misread—especially when documents conflict or are outdated. Prompts that do not require evidence, plus no confidence threshold or abstention behavior, can also lead the model to guess. For example, a policy answer may miss an exception stored in a separate table.

pregunta: How does RAG compare with a traditional enterprise search tool, and when would it be worth adding generative AI to the search experience?
respuesta: Traditional enterprise search retrieves and ranks documents, leaving employees to open files and synthesize answers. RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) first finds relevant, permitted sources, then uses a language model to produce a concise, contextual answer with citations. Add generative AI when people need answers across scattered documents, summaries, or comparisons—for example, finding a policy and explaining how it applies. Keep traditional search when users mainly need exact documents, speed, predictable results, or minimal cost; use RAG only with strong access controls and source verification.

pregunta: How could a Chilean retailer use an LLM to help customer-service agents without letting it make decisions on its own?
respuesta: A Chilean retailer could connect an LLM to approved product, delivery, and returns information so it can summarize customer conversations and draft suggested replies in Spanish. Agents review and edit each reply before sending. Keep decisions—such as refunds, exchanges, and complaint outcomes—with staff, and require human approval for any account changes. Log suggestions and approvals, and route uncertain or sensitive cases to a supervisor.

pregunta: What’s the difference between a zero-shot prompt and a few-shot prompt, and when would each be useful for a Chilean retailer?
respuesta: A zero-shot prompt gives the AI an instruction without examples—for instance, “Classify this customer message as a complaint, question, or compliment.” It’s useful for common, straightforward tasks such as summarizing sales reports. A few-shot prompt includes a handful of example inputs and desired outputs, helping the AI follow a specific style or classification rule. A Chilean retailer could use examples to tag local customer messages consistently, including Chilean slang or store-specific return categories.
